questions.text: Quick Revision - Electric Current and Ohm's Law

definitionBean.title: Electric Current and Ohm's Law
definitionBean.definition: The rate of flow of charge is called 'electric current'; and the current flowing through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across its ends, known as 'Ohm's Law'[cite: 39].
definitionBean.explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A). According to Ohm's law, V = IR, where V is potential difference, I is electric current, and R is resistance. The unit of resistance is the Ohm (Ω).
importantPoints: Ohm's Law: V is proportional to I or V = IR
Resistivity: Property of the conductor's material

questions.text: Quick Revision - Combination of Resistors and Electric Power

definitionBean.title: Combination of Resistors and Electric Power
definitionBean.definition: Resistors in a circuit are primarily connected in two ways - series ($R = R_1 + R_2$) and parallel ($\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2}$); and the rate of doing work is called electric power[cite: 39].
definitionBean.explanation: In a series connection, total resistance increases and current remains the same, whereas in a parallel connection, total resistance decreases and potential difference remains the same. The formula for electric power is $P = VI = I^2R = \frac{V^2}{R}$[cite: 39].
importantPoints: Series combination: Equivalent resistance Rs = R1 + R2 + R3

questions.text: Subject: Electric Current and Ohm's Law

parts.statement: State Ohm's law and draw the necessary electric circuit diagram for its verification[cite: 39].
parts.correct_answer: Current flowing through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference ($V = IR$)[cite: 39].
parts.explanation: According to Ohm's law, provided the physical conditions (such as temperature) remain unchanged, the electric current flowing through a metallic wire is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends ($V = IR$)[cite: 39].

parts.statement: Define electric current and potential difference, and state their SI units[cite: 39].
parts.correct_answer: Rate of flow of charge is electric current (Ampere), work done per unit charge is potential difference (Volt)[cite: 39].
parts.explanation: The rate of flow of charge is called electric current (Unit: Ampere); the work done in bringing a unit charge from one point to another is called potential difference (Unit: Volt)[cite: 39].

questions.text: Subject: Combination of Resistors and Power

parts.statement: Derive the expression for equivalent resistance when resistors are connected in series[cite: 39].
parts.correct_answer: Equivalent resistance in series is $R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$[cite: 39].
parts.explanation: When two or more resistors are connected end-to-end such that the second end of one connects to the first end of the next, it is called a series connection. The equivalent resistance is $R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$[cite: 39].

parts.statement: What is electric power? Write its various formulas and state its SI unit[cite: 39].
parts.correct_answer: Rate of energy consumption is electric power ($P = VI$), unit is Watt[cite: 39].
parts.explanation: The rate at which energy is consumed in an electric circuit is called electric power. Formulas: P = VI = I²R = V²/R. Its SI unit is the Watt.
